title: Extended Data Table 2 | Operating points and referral results for haemoglobin below 12 g/dL.
legend: **Extended Data Table 2 | Operating points and referral results for haemoglobin below 12 g/dL.** **a**, Every cut rule for every setting of Fig. 4e and Extended Data Fig. 5h, whole blood count hidden, with cuts set in the training folds. Referred, found and missed are per 1,000 people evaluated. **b**, Development contrasts and the AI-READI official test split, scored once, a previously accessed paired check because a predecessor model decoded these blood counts. n, ≥1,880 development people (five-fold cross-validation, ≥160 below 12 g/dL) and ≥340 test people (≥20 below 12 g/dL), floored to 20. Bootstrap 95% intervals hold scores, risk maps and cuts fixed. Only net benefit at 0.10 and haemoglobin MAE carry prespecified criteria, judged on an interval bound, and no hypothesis tests were run. The retinal net benefit gain met its criterion in development but not on the test, where it fell in the deployed fold 0 model, while the five-fold haemoglobin criterion was met. At 90% specificity the retina did not raise cases found. AI-READI is a selected, diabetes-enriched population, not a screening population, so PPV, NPV, yield and net benefit depend on its case mix. Risk maps and cuts were not fully nested, and 12 g/dL is not sex specific because sex is not held. Haemoglobin below 11 g/dL is PLACEHOLDER (fewer than 50 in a class). PPV and NPV, positive and negative predictive value. AUROC, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. MAE, mean absolute error.

methods_notes.a: Every operating point shown reached its target. The age-only reference at 90% specificity and at the matched flag rate is suppressed because a cell of the confusion table held fewer than 20 people. Differences between operating points are descriptive.
methods_notes.b: Net benefit at 0.10 was 0.031 [0.020, 0.041] for BRAN with retina, 0.023 [0.013, 0.033] for BRAN without retina, 0.019 [0.009, 0.029] for Retina and age, 0.035 [0.024, 0.046] for Ridge, clinical, retina, age, 0.026 [0.016, 0.036] for Ridge, clinical and age, 0.020 [0.009, 0.030] for Ridge, retina and age, against −0.011 [−0.026, 0.003] for treat all. At 90% specificity Retina and age minus BRAN without retina was −12 [−21, −4] cases found per 1,000 and Retina and age minus Ridge, age and predicted sex +7 [1, 15]. At 80% sensitivity BRAN with retina minus BRAN without retina was −72 [−90, −52] people referred per 1,000, with a sensitivity difference of 0.000 [−0.065, 0.067] and a specificity difference of +0.079 [0.059, 0.099], and Ridge, clinical, retina, age minus Ridge, clinical and age was −69 [−88, −48], so raw retinal features in a ridge model also lowered referrals. The two savings were not compared directly. Official test net benefit at 0.10, fold 0 deployed model 0.0468 with the retina and 0.0611 without, five-fold mean 0.0565 and 0.0487. The five-fold recalibration was fitted on single-model predictions, so that row carries no criterion. Haemoglobin MAE 0.911 g/dL with the retina and 0.973 without. Official test AUROC below 12 g/dL from the five-fold ensemble was 0.829 [0.755, 0.894] with the retina and 0.797 [0.724, 0.863] without, descriptive and not drawn.
